title: Christopher Nolan Chose Mumbai for His First-Ever India Premiere — and ₹3,300 IMAX Tickets Are Already Gone
excerpt: Matt Damon, Tom Holland, and the world's first all-IMAX epic head to Phoenix Palladium next month. For the diaspora, the July 17 release is the event to plan around.
body:
Here's what no one expected to type this year: **Christopher Nolan** is coming to Mumbai.

<youtube></youtube>

Not for a film-festival Q&A. Not for a hotel-ballroom panel with other directors. For a full-dress, red-carpet, stars-in-tow premiere of **The Odyssey**, his adaptation of Homer's ancient epic — and it will be the first time any Nolan film has ever held an official premiere in India.


![Phoenix Palladium — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3e/Lower_Parel_Phoenix_Palladium.jpg)



> **"Given that every Nolan film since *The Dark Knight* has opened to both critical and commercial triumph, it's not much of a gamble."**



**Universal Pictures** has placed Mumbai on the same global tour circuit as London, Paris, and New York. That sentence alone tells you where the Indian market stands in 2026. Nolan will be joined by **Matt Damon** (who plays Odysseus, the war-weary King of Ithaca), **Tom Holland** (his son Telemachus), and producer **Emma Thomas**, at the **PVR Icon IMAX at Phoenix Palladium** — the only venue in the country grand enough for the occasion.

And the occasion is enormous. *The Odyssey* isn't just another blockbuster with a pretty cast. It is the **first feature film ever shot entirely on IMAX cameras**. Every single frame. Not selected battle sequences, not the hero's climactic third-act charge — the whole thing, start to finish, captured on Nolan's beloved large-format stock. He has spent decades inching toward this moment: IMAX bursts in *The Dark Knight*, expanded sequences in *Interstellar*, the full-frame commitment of *Oppenheimer*. Now there are no standard fallback shots left. What you see on that towering screen is what the camera saw, in the widest, most detail-saturated format cinema has ever produced.

The cast, even by Nolan standards, is absurd. Beyond Damon and Holland, the film features **Anne Hathaway** as the steadfast Penelope, **Zendaya** as Athena, **Robert Pattinson** as Antinous (the leader of the suitors), **Charlize Theron** as the nymph Calypso, and **Lupita Nyong'o** pulling double duty as Helen of Troy and Clytemnestra. Somewhere in that list is every Best Picture speech from the last decade. The ensemble alone would sell tickets; the IMAX-only proposition turns it into an event.


![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)


And Indian audiences are treating it like one. IMAX advance bookings opened on June 8, and premium seats in Mumbai and Pune are being listed at **₹3,000 to ₹3,300** — some of the most expensive cinema tickets ever sold in the country. Late-night screenings sold out almost instantly. The price point has sparked debate, but the demand hasn't flinched. India's multiplex audience has made its position clear: they will pay a premium for a genuinely premium experience.

The premiere carries symbolic weight that extends well beyond Nolan's personal fandom. For years, India was a market Hollywood acknowledged in press releases but rarely visited for launches. That's been shifting — Tom Cruise's *Mission: Impossible* promotions in Mumbai, Marvel's growing India-first strategies — but a Nolan premiere in India is a different tier entirely. This is a director who could premiere anywhere on Earth, and he's choosing Mumbai alongside London and New York. Universal isn't doing this out of charity. India is now a first-week revenue engine, and Nolan's films have consistently overperformed here — *Oppenheimer* earned over ₹110 crore domestically, a staggering number for a three-hour subtitled drama about nuclear physics.

> "This is not just about box office collections. It's about establishing a direct connection with one of the most passionate movie-going audiences in the world."

Universal has also made headlines for its decision to **skip influencer screenings entirely** for *The Odyssey*, showing the film only to professional critics ahead of release. In an era where paid-enthusiasm previews generate suspiciously glowing social media reactions — *Supergirl* being the most recent cautionary tale — Nolan and Universal are betting that the work speaks for itself. Given that every Nolan film since *The Dark Knight* has opened to both critical and commercial triumph, it's not much of a gamble.

**For the diaspora**, the July 17 worldwide release means simultaneous access across the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East. The film will play in IMAX, standard, Dolby, and premium formats globally. If there was ever a film designed to be experienced on the biggest screen within driving distance, this is it. Skip the couch. Find your nearest IMAX. And if you happen to be in Mumbai next month — there's a red carpet with your favourite filmmaker's name on it.
